result.chapter_title: Major Reversal Price Patterns (Construction, Geometry & Math)
result.content:
The Double Bottom ('W' Pattern) is one of the highest-performing bullish reversal formations:
        - Construction: Two distinct troughs at approximately the same support level (within 2-3% tolerance). The first trough forms on heavy panic selling volume. An intervening reaction rally produces a peak (the neckline). A secondary decline retests the support zone of the first trough on noticeably lighter volume, showing seller depletion.
        - Confluence: Often accompanied by bullish RSI or MACD divergence (RSI makes a higher low while price makes an equal or slightly lower low).
        - Confirmation: The pattern is confirmed only when price penetrates and closes above the intervening peak neckline on a surge of volume.
        - Measuring Target Formula: Measure the vertical height H from the lowest trough to the intervening peak neckline. Project H upward from the neckline breakout: Target Price = Neckline + H.
        - Protective Stop: Place stop-loss just below the lowest low of the two troughs or below the right trough low.

rules.text: Enter long when price closes above the neckline with volume ratio > 1.35x.
Stop-Loss is positioned 1.0x ATR below the second trough low.

result.chapter_title: Major Reversal Price Patterns (Construction, Geometry & Math)
result.content:
The Double Top ('M' Pattern) is a prominent reversal formation occurring at market cycle peaks:
        - Construction: Two prominent price peaks at approximately the same level (within 2-3% price difference). The first peak forms on heavy buying volume. A decline of 10-20% follows, creating an intervening trough (the neckline support). A second rally lifts price back to the resistance level of the first peak, but on significantly lower volume. Price fails to break through and rolls over.
        - Confirmation: The pattern is NOT confirmed when the second peak fails; it is confirmed ONLY when price decisively penetrates and closes below the intervening trough neckline.
        - Measuring Target Formula: Measure the vertical height H between the peaks and the neckline trough. Project H downward from the neckline breakout point: Target Price = Neckline - H.
        - Protective Stop: Place protective stop-loss slightly above the second peak or 1.2x ATR above the neckline.

rules.text: Never short until price produces a confirmed close below the intervening neckline trough.
Stop-Loss is positioned above Peak 2 high.

tool_log.query: Inverse Head and Shoulders pattern target stop loss rules

result.chapter_title: Major Reversal Price Patterns (Construction, Geometry & Math)
result.section_title: Inverse Head and Shoulders Bottom Formation
result.content:
The Inverse Head and Shoulders (Head and Shoulders Bottom) signals the exhaustion of a downtrend and the birth of a major bullish trend:
        - Construction: Features three distinct price troughs. The Left Shoulder trough forms after a sharp selloff on heavy volume. An upward reaction forms the neckline resistance. The Head forms as price plummets to a lower low on moderate volume. Price rebounds back to the neckline. The Right Shoulder trough forms at a higher low than the head (often roughly level with the left shoulder) on light volume, demonstrating that sellers are exhausted.
        - Volume Characteristics: Volume expands during the advance out of the head, dries up during the right shoulder trough, and must explode into an unmistakable volume surge as price crosses the neckline.
        - Measuring Target Formula: Measure the vertical distance from the bottom of the Head to the Neckline (Height H). Project this distance upward from the Neckline breakout point: Target Price = Neckline Price + H.
        - Protective Stop: Place protective stop-loss just below the low of the Right Shoulder or 1.2x ATR below the broken neckline.

rules.text: Initiate long position upon an hourly close above the neckline with a volume surge (>1.35x average).
Set Stop-Loss just below the Right Shoulder trough low.

result.chapter_title: Major Reversal Price Patterns (Construction, Geometry & Math)
result.content:
The Head and Shoulders Top is the most reliable major reversal pattern in technical analysis. It signals the transition from an established uptrend to a downtrend:
        - Construction: Consists of three distinct price peaks. The Left Shoulder forms on high volume as the uptrend continues. Price corrects to form the neckline support. The Head forms on another rally reaching a higher peak than the left shoulder, but often with noticeably lighter volume (divergence). Price declines back to test neckline support. The Right Shoulder forms on a weaker rally that fails to reach the height of the head, accompanied by sharply declining volume.
        - Neckline: Drawn by connecting the reaction lows between the left shoulder and head, and the head and right shoulder. It can be horizontal, upward-sloping, or downward-sloping (downward sloping necklines are extremely bearish).
        - Volume Characteristics: Volume is highest during the left shoulder, lower on the head, lowest during the right shoulder, and surges violently when price breaks below the neckline.
        - Measuring Target Formula: Measure the vertical distance from the peak of the Head straight down to the Neckline (Pattern Height H). Project this distance downward from the Neckline breakout point: Target Price = Neckline Price - H.
        - Protective Stop: Place initial stop-loss just above the peak of the Right Shoulder or 1.5x ATR above the broken neckline.

rules.text: Enter short only after a decisive candle close below the neckline with expanding volume.
Set Stop-Loss above the high of the Right Shoulder.
